title: Organic chemistry: isomerism, alkynes, benzene, ethers and C=O - 123 school
heading: Organic chemistry: isomerism, alkynes, benzene, ethers and C=O
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: What is the general formula of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes (open chain)?
questions.a: Alkanes: C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>, alkenes: C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>, alkynes: C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n–2</sub>

questions.q: Which group is characteristic of alkynes?
questions.a: The triple bond C≡C

questions.q: Give the name and molecular formula of the simplest alkyne
questions.a: Ethyne, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub>

questions.q: Give the molecular formula of hex-1-yne
questions.a: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>10</sub>

questions.q: How many moles of Br<sub>2</sub> can 1 mol of ethyne take up at most and what is the product then?
questions.a: 2 mol of Br<sub>2</sub>. The product is 1,1,2,2-tetrabromoethane

questions.q: How many moles of H<sub>2</sub> are needed to convert 1 mol of ethyne completely into ethane?
questions.a: 2 mol: C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub> + 2 H<sub>2</sub> → C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>

questions.q: What are cycloalkanes and what is their general formula?
questions.a: Hydrocarbons with a ring of single C–C bonds. General formula C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>

questions.q: Give the molecular formula of cyclohexane
questions.a: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>

questions.q: Which kind of hydrocarbon is an isomer of cyclohexane?
questions.a: Hex-1-ene (an alkene with formula C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>)

questions.q: How can you distinguish between cyclohexane and cyclohexene with bromine water?
questions.a: Cyclohexene decolourises bromine water (addition), cyclohexane does not

questions.q: What is the molecular formula of benzene and what does the molecule look like?
questions.a: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>6</sub>. A flat ring of 6 C atoms with all C–C bonds equally long

questions.q: Does benzene react easily with bromine water like alkenes?
questions.a: No. Benzene does not decolourise bromine water. It does react with bromine under other conditions, for example with a catalyst, by substitution

questions.q: What is a phenyl group?
questions.a: A benzene ring of which one H atom is replaced by a bond to the rest of the molecule: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>–

questions.q: Give the molecular formula of bromobenzene
questions.a: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>Br

questions.q: What is an ether and which group does it contain?
questions.a: A substance with an oxygen atom between two carbon atoms: C–O–C

questions.q: Give the name of CH<sub>3</sub>–O–CH<sub>3</sub>
questions.a: Methoxymethane

questions.q: Give the name of CH<sub>3</sub>–O–CH<sub>2</sub>–CH<sub>3</sub>
questions.a: Methoxyethane

questions.q: Why does methoxymethane have a much lower boiling point than ethanol (same molecular formula)?
questions.a: Methoxymethane has no OH group. The molecules form no hydrogen bonds with each other

questions.q: Which group do aldehydes and ketones have in common, and what is the difference?
questions.a: Both have a C=O group. In an aldehyde the C=O is at the end of the chain (CHO), in a ketone the C=O is inside the chain

questions.q: Give the name of CH<sub>3</sub>–CH<sub>2</sub>–CHO and of CH<sub>3</sub>–CO–CH<sub>3</sub>
questions.a: Propanal and propanone

questions.q: Give the name of CH<sub>3</sub>–CO–CH<sub>2</sub>–CH<sub>2</sub>–CH<sub>3</sub>
questions.a: Pentan-2-one

questions.q: What are structural isomers?
questions.a: Substances with the same molecular formula but a different structural formula

questions.q: Name three structural isomers of C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>12</sub>
questions.a: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane
questions.e: If you have two of the three right, it counts as correct.

questions.q: Which two kinds of substances with the molecular formula C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O are structural isomers of each other?
questions.a: Propanal (aldehyde) and propanone (ketone)

questions.q: What is stereoisomerism?
questions.a: Substances with the same structural formula but a different spatial arrangement of the atoms

questions.q: Which two conditions must a molecule meet to have cis/trans isomerism?
questions.a: There is a C=C (or ring) and each C atom of that bond carries two different groups

questions.q: Does but-2-ene have cis/trans isomerism? And but-1-ene?
questions.a: But-2-ene does (cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene), but-1-ene does not (two H atoms on one C of the double bond)

questions.q: What is an asymmetric C atom?
questions.a: A C atom with four different groups attached

questions.q: Which of these substances has an asymmetric C atom: butan-2-ol or propan-2-ol?
questions.a: Butan-2-ol (C-2 has H, OH, CH<sub>3</sub> and C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>). In propan-2-ol there are two equal CH<sub>3</sub> groups on C-2

questions.q: What are enantiomers?
questions.a: Two molecules that are mirror images of each other and cannot be superimposed. They arise at an asymmetric C atom

questions.q: What is the same and what is different in two enantiomers?
questions.a: Nearly all properties (boiling point, solubility) are equal. They rotate polarised light in opposite directions and can act differently in the body

questions.q: A molecule has 3 asymmetric C atoms. What is the maximum number of stereoisomers?
questions.a: 2<sup>3</sup> = 8

questions.q: What is the connection between lactic acid (2-hydroxypropanoic acid) and enantiomers?
questions.a: C-2 has four different groups (H, OH, CH<sub>3</sub>, COOH), so lactic acid has two enantiomers
